text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS
- The Supreme Court has summoned reporters and editors of three Urdu dailies to appear before the Chief Justice in his chamber on misreporting the arrest of main Shi'ite leader Allama Sajid Naqvi.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said the government has no intentions to probe into foreign currency accounts and called upon the people to retain their accounts within the country.
DAWN
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif appealed to businessmen to boost exports and share part of their profit with others by paying taxes to consolidate the economy of the country.
- Pakistan would like political conflicts such as Kashmir to be resolved before further opening up its economy within the SAARC region, Commerce Minister Ishaq Dar said.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the state's Corporate Law Authority was being restructured into an autonomous body.
- The governor of the State (central) Bank of Pakistan warned that Pakistan will be in deep trouble if businessmen fail to pay their taxes honestly and revenue is not collected in time.
- State-run Habib Bank Ltd (HBL) will be privatised within 12 to 18 months, HBL President Shaukat Tarin said.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz asked spinners to reduce export of cotton yarn by half and utilise the quantity in the production of other value-added textile products.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz refused to offer further incentives to the textile sector, such as a ban on raw cotton export, devaluation of the rupee and export financing facility to cotton yarn of 30 counts.
- To eliminate the monopoly of a few firms on gold import the Ministry of Commerce will invite bids for the import of gold in the next few days, sources said.
- Commerce Minister Ishaq Dar said SAARC members should chalk out a strategy to fight Western bloc plans to impose anti-dumping duties on South Asian exports.
THE NATION
- Pakistan will get the first $200 million tranche of the IMF loan by mid-October.
THE FRONTIER POST

- The anti-terrorist law enacted by the government in a hurry will usurp fundamental human rights enshrined in the constitution and give police a licence to kill, said parliamentarians of the ethnic Mutahida Qaumi Movement (MQM).
THE MUSLIM
- Representatives of bar bodies termed the new anti-terrorism legislation as a black law and the special courts to be established under that act as worse than martial law courts.
- Okara, a city in southern Punjab, has been handed over to the paramilitary rangers to check growing sectarian violence.
- German Deputy Defence Minister Bernd Wilz reached Islamabad on Monday at the head of three-member defence delegation on a six-day official visit to Pakistan.
